subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@finhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — good to meet you and learn more about FinHealth's use cases. Below is a short recap and the next steps we discussed. Please flag anything I've misunderstood.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Regulated PHI workloads across telehealth and claims: zero-tolerance for uncontrolled egress and strict auditability (HIPAA).
- Need customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) and full control over key lifecycle.
- Some clinics require an air-gapped/isolated deployment model for offline sites.
- Strong requirement for data residency (US-only) and 7+ year audit log retention.
- Production SLAs: target 99.9% uptime for inference, p95 generation latency < 300ms for short prompts, throughput ~20 qps for peak periods.

Current stack (from our notes)
- Primary infra: AWS (us-east-1 / us-west-2), EKS for services, S3 for long-term storage.
- Identity: Okta SSO (SAML) across apps.
- Networking: strict outbound egress rules; only managed NAT for a subset of services; central firewall team.

Success criteria for an initial POC
- Private/VPC deployment with data plane inside FinHealth VPC and no public egress for model inputs/outputs.
- Customer-managed KMS or HSM integration for at-rest and in-transit keys.
- Demonstrated inference for a representative workload (billing/claims redaction + chat triage) with latency/throughput targets met.
- Delivery of SOC2 artifacts and security questionnaire answers.

Open items / risks
- Exact HSM model and whether FIPS-validated HSM is required.
- Whether an on-prem air-gapped appliance is required for specific clinic sites.
- Procurement/contract cadence and budget window (Q2).

Next steps (agreed)
1) Schedule a technical SE session to go through network and deploy options (PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs on-prem). Proposed: Thu 2026-03-14 11:00 AM PT.
2) I will send our security questionnaire and a short checklist of network prerequisites (attached).
3) SE (Aditya) will prepare a draft architecture options doc and ballpark sizing for GPUs & cost.
4) Procurement (cc'ed) to start reviewing NDA / procurement terms; Marissa to follow up with standard procurement template.

Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf, network_diagram.png

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — that looks right from our side. A few clarifications:
- We absolutely need customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS backed by our HSM) for all model artifacts and logs containing PHI.
- For air-gapped sites, we're likely to require a deployable appliance (no internet) for a small subset of clinics; can Redwood support an offline update process?
- Network-wise we prefer PrivateLink over peering where possible because of central networking policy.

Procurement is looped in to start the paperwork. Can you also provide a ballpark for POC pricing (4-week engagement, one medium GPU instance pool + SE time)? If you can share a short cost estimate ahead of the SE call that will help speed internal approvals.

I'll attach the network diagram we referenced.

On Thu 3/14 11am PT works for me.

Thanks,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Appreciate the notes, Alex. Quick technical follow-up and options so the SE call can be focused: 

1) Deployment patterns (pros/cons)
- PrivateLink (recommended): minimal routing changes, keeps control plane in Redwood, data plane traffic stays within AWS backbone. Works well with strict egress policies.
- VPC Peering: lower latency but requires peering approvals from your networking team and cross-account routing rules.
- On-prem / air-gapped appliance: We offer an on-prem bundle; updates are delivered via signed bundles your security team can approve. This path requires longer setup and an approval window for offline update operations.

2) KMS/HSM
- We support AWS KMS keys in customer accounts and integration with cloud HSM (e.g., AWS CloudHSM). For FIPS/HSM appliances on-prem, we can work with your HSM vendor; will need HSM model and admin access window during setup.

3) Network prerequisites
- Whitelist IP ranges for our control-plane endpoints (we'll provide a short list).
- Allow PrivateLink endpoints and necessary VPC endpoints (S3 if you'd like us to use S3 in your account for model artifacts).
- DNS resolution: allow internal DNS names for our service endpoints; if you enforce strict DNS, we'll provide alternate hostnames.

4) Sizing & performance
- For the use cases discussed (short prompt generation + light batching), a small pool of A10x-like GPUs (or equivalent) should meet 20 qps with p95 < 300ms when properly tuned. Final sizing depends on average prompt length and concurrency distribution; we'll baseline during POC.

I'll bring a short deployment options slide to the SE call and a checklist for network/security pre-reqs. I can also draft a 4-week POC cost estimate and share before the call.

- Aditya
